chalisa.do1: Bowing my head to the Arihantas, I offer salutation to the Siddhas, and take the joy-giving names of the Upādhyāyas and Ācāryas.
chalisa.do2: Bowing too to all the sādhus, to Sarasvatī and to the joy-giving Jina temples, I hold Lord Mahāvīra in the temple of my mind.
chalisa.cau1: Victory to you, Mahāvīra, merciful Lord. Lord Vīra, you are renowned in the world. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: Vardhamāna is your name; it feels most dear to the heart. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: Your image is peaceful and your form enchanting; your lovely face is full of dignity and smiling. ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: You took the sky-clad guise of a digambara; even the enemy karma was defeated by you. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: You drove away anger, pride and greed; great delusion grew afraid of you. ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: You are omniscient, the knower of all; what bond have you with the world? ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: In you there is neither attachment nor hatred; you are the hero in the battle with attachment, the teacher of what is good. ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: Your name in the world is true, a name every child knows. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: Ghosts and spirits are afraid of you; vyantaras (wandering spirits) and demons all run away. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: Great sickness and plague cause no torment; Death, most dreadful, is afraid. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: Be it a black, hooded cobra, or a huge and fearsome lion, ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: and should there be no one to save, then, Lord, you alone protect. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: Should a forest fire be smouldering and blazing up in a strong wind, ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: your name takes away all sorrow, and the fire turns cool at once. ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: All Bhārata was full of violence; then you brought it deliverance. ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: You were born in the city of Kuṇḍalapura; then all the people were happy. ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: Siddhārtha was your father; you were the apple of Triśalā's eye. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: Leaving all worldly entanglements, the Lord became a celibate from boyhood. ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: In the fifth age, a time of great sorrow, you showed your glory at Cāṁdanapura. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: In a mound you showed a wonder (atiśaya): you made a cow's milk flow there. ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: Worry arose in the cowherd's mind; he came there with a spade. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: He dug away the whole mound and cast it aside; then you gave your darśana. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: Trouble beset Jodharāja; when he chanted your name, ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: the cannonball turned cold; then everyone raised the cry of victory. ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: The minister had a temple built; the king too spent wealth on it. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: A large rest-house was built, and it was settled to bring you. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: You broke scores of carts; the wheel did not budge forward. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: When the cowherd put his hand to it, the chariot was then found moving. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: On the first day of the dark fortnight of Vaiśākha, the chariot goes to the bank of the river. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: The Mīṇās and Gujars all come; dancing and leaping, their hearts all swell with joy. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: Lord, you kept faith with love, and greatly raised the cowherd's honour. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: Only when the cowherd's hand touches it, Lord, does the chariot move. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: My boat is all but broken; without you there is no one to row it across. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Lord, show me a little grace; I am your servant, Lord. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: I want nothing else from you; may I have your darśana birth after birth. ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: Candra composes this Chālīsā and bows his head to Lord Vīra. ॥36॥
chalisa.so1: Whoever recites it forty times a day for forty days, burning fragrant incense without measure before Vardhamāna,
chalisa.so2: if he is poor from birth, becomes like Kubera; if he has no children, his name and line carry on in the world.
